articles.title: After invasive rainbow trout threaten to erase Yellowstone’s native cutthroat fish, officials shut Buffalo Creek to wipe them out
articles.summary: US News: Yellowstone National Park is preparing to temporarily close part of Buffalo Creek as wildlife officials launch a targeted effort to remove invasive ra.
articles.body: Yellowstone National Park is preparing to temporarily close part of Buffalo Creek as wildlife officials launch a targeted effort to remove invasive rainbow trout threatening native fish populations. The conservation operation will begin on August 31, with the northern section of Buffalo Creek remaining closed to visitors until September 7 while biologists treat the waterway. According to NBC Montana, the park will use rotenone, an EPA-approved piscicide, to eliminate the invasive fish from the creek. Yellowstone National Park said the work is intended to protect Yellowstone cutthroat trout, the only trout species native to the park, from competition and hybridisation. The project forms part of a broader native fish conservation programme aimed at protecting the ecological health of the Lamar River watershed.Yellowstone closes Buffalo Creek for invasive trout removalBeginning August 31, Buffalo Creek will be temporarily closed from the northern Yellowstone boundary downstream to its confluence with Slough Creek. The closure is scheduled to last until September 7, allowing fisheries biologists to carry out the treatment without public access to the affected stretch. Yellowstone National Park said the operation will target invasive rainbow trout using rotenone, a piscicide approved by the US Environmental Protection Agency. The park has also confirmed that the treatment will not affect the potability of water at Slough Creek Campground, where drinking water will remain safe. Signs will be posted to alert visitors to the temporary restrictions. The announcement comes as Yellowstone continues efforts to prevent nonnative fish from spreading through sensitive waterways and undermining long-term native fish restoration projects.Invasive rainbow trout threaten Yellowstone cutthroat troutThe Buffalo Creek operation is focused on a population of invasive rainbow trout that has become a source of fish entering nearby waterways. According to Yellowstone National Park, these rainbow trout compete and hybridise with native Yellowstone cutthroat trout in Slough Creek, Soda Butte Creek and the Lamar River. This creates both ecological and genetic concerns because hybridisation can weaken the genetic integrity of native cutthroat populations. Yellowstone cutthroat trout are the only trout species native to the park and play an important ecological role across the Greater Yellowstone Ecosystem. The National Park Service says genetically pure populations have declined across their natural range because of competition, predation, hybridisation and habitat degradation. Removing the source population in Buffalo Creek is therefore considered crucial to maintaining the native trout population in the Lamar River watershed.Why Yellowstone uses rotenone to control invasive fishRotenone is not a new tool in Yellowstone's fight against nonnative fish. The National Park Service says piscicides such as rotenone are used because they can selectively target fish while conservation teams take steps to minimise impacts on other aquatic organisms. Before treatment, biologists survey the area and use the lowest effective concentration, while chemical use is timed to reduce risks to amphibians and other wildlife. Any native Yellowstone cutthroat trout captured through electrofishing before the Buffalo Creek project will be moved outside the treatment zone. Yellowstone has previously used rotenone during native fish restoration efforts, including projects in the Soda Butte Creek drainage. Those efforts have helped remove invasive populations and create conditions in which native cutthroat trout can recover.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Mohan Bhagwat in US: Hindu American Foundation issues security advisory ahead of RSS event
articles.summary: India News: American non-profit organisation, The Hindu American Foundation has issued an advisory ahead of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh's event in New York City, .
articles.body: American non-profit organisation, The Hindu American Foundation has issued an advisory ahead of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh's event in New York City, advising citizens to stay vigilant, aware, and civilised."HAF is issuing this security alert in advance of the Universal Oneness Celebration at Madison Square Garden in New York City. Stay vigilant, remain situationally aware, and keep interactions civil. Ahead of the event, activists targeting Hindu Americans have attempted to disrupt and cancel the celebration", HAF posted on X, while also urging New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani to ensure the safety of the event attendees.The community advisory was issued after intense criticism of the RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and his 'Universal Oneness Celebration', to be held on Saturday at Madison Square Garden.On Tuesday, Mamdani expressed his lack of support for Bhagwat's event while admitting his office cannot cancel it.“I don’t support the rally, but I don’t know if the city has any jurisdiction on cancelling a private event,” he told reporters.United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) asked US government to consider sanctions against the RSS, alleging deterioration of religious freedom in India."We urge the US government to consider targeted sanctions against RSS members and Indian officials complicit in religious freedom violations, including revoking the visa issued to Mohan Bhagwat and making him ineligible for future entry into the United States", the body said.The USCIRF is Chaired by Pakistani-American Asif Mahmood.The body has previously been dismissed by the ministry of external affairs over bias and lack of credibility."We all know this is a biased institution. For years, it has made incorrect and provocative statements about India. We should ignore such institutions, as they have their own agendas and lack credibility", MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said during an August 21 press briefing.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Birmingham weather forecast: Heavy rain expected August 27, 2026
articles.summary: UK News: Birmingham residents are bracing for a wet start to their week as heavy rain is forecast for August 27, 2026, with overcast skies and a significant ch.
articles.body: Birmingham residents are bracing for a wet start to their week as heavy rain is forecast for August 27, 2026, with overcast skies and a significant chance of precipitation. Temperatures will remain mild throughout the day, with a high of 20°C and a low of 14°C, and humidity expected to reach 98%. Wind speeds will be around 33.8 kph. Looking ahead, the weather is expected to improve gradually, with light rain on August 28, transitioning back to heavy rain on August 29, before shifting to sunny intervals from August 30 through September 1, and concluding with cloudy skies on September 2.The day in Birmingham will be dominated by heavy rain, with the skies expected to remain largely overcast throughout the day. The maximum temperature is predicted to reach 20°C, while the minimum temperature will hover around 14°C. The average temperature for the day is anticipated to be 17.0°C. Humidity levels are expected to be high, reaching 98%, contributing to the damp conditions. There is a 10% chance of rain, but the forecast indicates heavy rain, suggesting that any precipitation could be significant. Wind speeds are expected to be around 33.8 kph, adding a brisk element to the otherwise muggy atmosphere.Resident AdvisoryWith heavy rain expected throughout the day, residents are strongly advised to carry umbrellas and wear waterproof footwear. Outdoor plans may need to be adjusted, and it would be prudent to postpone any non-essential excursions until the weather improves. Commuters should allow for extra travel time due to potentially slippery roads and reduced visibility. Staying indoors and enjoying indoor activities is the most practical recommendation for today.Extended ForecastTomorrow, August 28, light rain is forecast, with temperatures remaining similar to today, with a high of 20°C and a low of 14°C. The rain is expected to transition to heavy rain again on August 29, with a high of 19°C and a low of 14°C. By August 30, the weather is predicted to shift towards sunny intervals, with temperatures reaching 21°C and dropping to 13°C. This trend of sunny intervals is expected to continue through September 1, with temperatures ranging between 18°C and 14°C. The week will conclude with cloudy skies on September 2, with a high of 20°C and a low of 15°C.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Over 76 lakh women registered under Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna: Punjab CM Mann
articles.summary: India News: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann on Wednesday said 76.11 lakh women have been registered under the state government's Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna.He.
articles.body: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann on Wednesday said 76.11 lakh women have been registered under the state government's Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna.He said a sum of Rs 2,381 crore has already been transferred into the accounts of 68.06 lakh women.Under the Mukh Mantri Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojana, women from the general category receive Rs 1,000 per month, while those belonging to the Scheduled Castes get Rs 1,500.Mann said the Punjab government's commitment to women's welfare would remain unwavering and the financial aid scheme for women would not be discontinued as long as the AAP remained in power in Punjab.He also said a sum of Rs 52.20 crore has been transferred to the accounts of 1.37 lakh 'Satkar Sakhis', while recognising their contribution in taking this scheme to women across Punjab.The chief minister said 'Satkar Sakhis' would receive Rs 300 for every registration, enabling them to earn more than Rs 200 crore through the initiative."'Satkar Sakhis' have played a crucial role in taking this scheme to women across Punjab. Their dedicated efforts have enabled more than 75 lakh women to get registered under the Mukh Mantri Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna," he said.Addressing a gathering virtually, Mann said his government launched the scheme in recognition of the dignity and respect of women.This financial assistance may not make women rich, but it will certainly provide them dignity and self-respect. Women deserve the highest respect because they are the source of life itself, and the blessings of mothers and sisters can help overcome every challenge in the world, he stated.Punjab AAP's women wing president and MLA Amandeep Kaur also lauded the dedicated contribution of 'Satkar Sakhis' and the entire women wing in taking the Mukh Mantri Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna to women across Punjab, saying they were not merely helping women fill forms but were becoming a source of support in transforming their lives.PTIGet the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 1933, Herbert Hoover donated Rapidan Camp to the federal government for Shenandoah National Park; today, the former presidential retreat sits less than 90 miles from Washington, DC
articles.summary: US News: Discover the history of Rapidan Camp, the presidential retreat of Herbert Hoover, donated to the federal government in 1933 for Shenandoah National Park. Learn about its significance and preservation efforts today.
articles.body: In 1933, as Herbert Hoover left the White House after losing re-election, he donated Rapidan Camp, his secluded Virginia mountain retreat, to the federal government for incorporation into the future Shenandoah National Park. Today, the Rapidan Camp remains within the park, while the National Park Service describes Shenandoah as less than 90 miles southwest of Washington, DC. The former presidential retreat preserves the unusual setting where Hoover combined fishing and recreation with his federal work during some of the most difficult years of the Great Depression.A mountain retreat that became a presidential campPresident Hoover and his wife, Lou Henry Hoover, established Rapidan Camp in 1929, shortly after Herbert Hoover took office. The camp stood at the headwaters of the Rapidan River in the Blue Ridge Mountains and included several other rustic buildings surrounded by forest. While fishing was reportedly one of the president's favourite pastimes, the site was not simply a holiday retreat. According to the National Park Service, Hoover conducted official business there and held meetings with visitors, thus creating a working presidential camp far removed from the formal surroundings of Washington.The property covered about 164 acres and was privately owned by the Hoovers during his time as the country’s president. Furthermore, the location held significance as it was situated within the landscape being considered for the creation of Shenandoah National Park. The president supported the park project and intended to make the future park accessible. The camp consequently became a place where presidential recreation and government business overlapped. Hoover could fish in the surrounding streams and escape the capital’s political pressure while still receiving visitors and dealing with matters of state. The NPS describes the camp as Hoover’s “summer White House,” reflecting its role as a presidential retreat during his administration.Hoover donated the camp to the future parkHoover lost his 1932 re-election campaign to Franklin D. Roosevelt, whose inauguration took place in March 1933. As the former president prepared to leave office, he offered Rapidan Camp to the federal government for use as a part of the proposed Shenandoah National Park. The NPS timeline records the donation in 1933, thus allowing the camp to become a part of the federal park landscape that was being assembled in Virginia.However, Shenandoah was not yet a national park when Hoover made the gift. Congress had authorised the park in 1926, but Virginia still had to acquire and transfer the necessary land before the federal government could formally establish it. The park was eventually established on 26 December 1935, and Roosevelt formally dedicated the park on 3 July 1936.Roosevelt himself visited the Rapidan Camp on 9 April 1933, shortly after his inauguration, anchoring the transition between Hoover’s retreat and its eventual incorporation into Shenandoah. This specific visit allowed him to assess the property during the interim period between Hoover's donation and the land's eventual integration into the national park system. The landscape around the camp was also being transformed by the park’s development and by work associated with the Civilian Conservation Corps.A decade after the park's formal establishment, the Shenandoah superintendent reported in 1946 that the camp was sitting unused, and subsequently sought funding either to repair the buildings or demolish them. Instead, the property acquired a new use. In 1948, the Boy Scouts of America received a 20-year lease to use the camp as a summer facility, a decision consistent with Hoover’s wishes for the property.Further rehabilitation took place between 1960 and 1963, and decades later the NPS carried out a restoration focused on historical accuracy. After decades of exposure had led to the dismantling of the site's temporary structures, in 2004, the agency completed the restoration of the grounds and the three surviving cabins associated with Hoover’s retreat: the Brown House, Prime Minister’s Cabin and the Creel Cabin. The agency’s work aimed to preserve the appearance and character of the camp during the Hoover years instead of leaving the buildings to deteriorate.Therefore, the preservation of Rapidan Camp offers a link to a pivotal era in American history. The historic cabins that would have otherwise deteriorated now stand as an educational resource in Shenandoah National Park, thus allowing modern visitors to explore the unique environment where a president found solace during the heights of the Great Depression.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
